title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate regarding the importance of religious freedom, authoritative texts, and transparency in artificial intelligence systems.
action: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4958; text: CR S4951)
summary: The Senate resolution emphasizes that artificial intelligence systems must respect religious freedom, draw on authoritative texts, and maintain transparency. It calls for policies that ensure AI development is open, accountable, and aligned with fundamental religious rights.

title: To direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress a report on the use of artificial intelligence systems to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy directs the Director of National Intelligence to submit a report to Congress detailing how artificial intelligence is used to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act’s Section 702. This report is intended to provide oversight and ensure compliance with surveillance laws regarding AI technologies.

title: To authorize certain labor market data collection activities and to improve Federal measurement of the workforce impacts of artificial intelligence, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This policy authorizes specific labor market data collection activities to better understand how artificial intelligence impacts employment. It also aims to improve federal measurement and reporting of AI’s workforce effects, addressing related concerns.

title: To require entities to include human-controlled shutdown mechanisms in all artificial intelligence systems.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The policy requires that every artificial‑intelligence system includes a shutdown mechanism that can be controlled by a human operator. This provision ensures that if an AI behaves unexpectedly or poses a danger, a person can immediately halt its operation.

title: To require the Secretary of Homeland Security to carry out prize competitions to advance the science of interpretability and to develop adversarial robustness with respect to artificial intelligence products, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The policy requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to run prize competitions that encourage research into making AI systems easier to understand and harder to attack. This aims to improve the safety, reliability, and security of AI technologies used by the U.S. government.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act seeks to shield consumers from misleading or fraudulent AI practices by setting clear standards for transparency and honesty. It requires companies to disclose when AI systems are used, provides mechanisms for consumers to verify claims, and imposes penalties for deceptive AI behavior.

title: A bill to establish the Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This bill proposes creating a new Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations to oversee and address emerging threats related to artificial intelligence and cyber attacks. It also outlines additional provisions to support national security, regulation, and collaboration across agencies and the private sector.

title: A bill to establish the Artificial Intelligence Horizon Fund, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The bill proposes creating a fund called the Artificial Intelligence Horizon Fund to support research, development, and innovation in artificial intelligence. It also includes additional provisions that aim to address related regulatory, ethical, and safety concerns for AI technologies.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act sets out rules for developing, testing, and deploying AI models to make sure they are safe, transparent, and ethically sound. It requires companies to explain how their AI systems work and to take responsibility for any harms that might arise from their use.

title: To establish a human-centered Federal framework for artificial intelligence in education and the workforce, promote the ethical and responsible teaching and learning of artificial intelligence, provide for equitable access to artificial intelligence-ready workforce development, safeguard student and worker data privacy, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy aims to build a federal, human‑centered framework for using artificial intelligence in education and the workforce, focusing on responsible development and implementation. It also seeks to ensure fair access to AI‑ready workforce training, protect privacy for students and workers, and promote ethical teaching and learning of AI.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act aims to shield households from the rising costs of electricity driven by large AI data centers. It proposes regulations or incentives to curb energy use, lower rates, or provide financial relief so families aren’t burdened by the growing demand for AI computing power.

title: Department of Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: The Department of Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence Act establishes a new federal department dedicated to advanced technology and AI. It outlines responsibilities for research, regulation, and coordination of AI initiatives across government agencies.

title: A bill to establish the Department of Artificial Intelligence and to provide for the regulation of advanced artificial intelligence systems, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This bill proposes creating a new Department of Artificial Intelligence to coordinate national AI policy. It also establishes rules to regulate advanced AI systems and addresses other related matters.

title: A bill to require disclosure of certain information relating to artificial intelligence systems, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The bill would mandate that developers and companies disclose key details about AI systems—like how they work, the data they use, and potential risks—so users and regulators can better understand them. It also includes other related measures to address the broader impacts and governance of AI technology.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 is a proposed law that aims to ensure AI technologies used to support veterans—such as in healthcare, benefits processing, and job training—are developed and deployed in ways that are ethical, transparent, and respectful of veterans’ rights. The act would establish guidelines, oversight mechanisms, and safeguards to protect veterans from bias, misuse, and privacy violations while fostering innovation that truly serves their needs.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act is a proposed law designed to curb the development and deployment of artificial intelligence systems that could act independently in ways that pose serious safety or security risks. It aims to impose strict regulations, oversight, and possibly bans on certain types of autonomous AI to protect public welfare.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act is designed to set clear rules and responsibilities for the artificial‑intelligence systems that review and decide veterans’ benefits claims. It calls for transparent data use, bias‑checking procedures, and independent oversight so veterans receive fair, accurate decisions.

title: Covered AI Prohibition Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Covered AI Prohibition Act would prohibit the use of certain AI systems in specific sectors. It seeks to protect critical areas by limiting the deployment of potentially harmful artificial intelligence technologies.

title: Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act establishes standards and processes for ensuring that artificial‑intelligence systems used by the military meet stringent reliability and safety requirements. It also requires regular reporting on AI performance, incidents, and risk assessments so that oversight bodies and policymakers can monitor and address potential issues.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 establishes rules to make sure that the Department of Veterans Affairs discloses when and how it uses artificial intelligence in its services. It also requires the VA to provide clear explanations of AI-driven decisions and safeguards for veterans’ privacy and data security.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The bill directs the Secretary of Homeland Security—working through the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency—to create a pilot program that tests AI tools for protecting critical infrastructure from cyber threats. It aims to explore how AI can strengthen cybersecurity defenses in essential services like energy, water, and communications.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act is a law designed to make artificial intelligence systems safer and more resilient, protecting them from hacking, misuse, or accidental harm. It sets out guidelines, testing rules, and oversight measures that developers and users must follow to identify and fix security risks before AI systems are widely deployed.

title: Ban AI Denials in Medicare Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Ways and Means, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Ban AI Denials in Medicare Act seeks to prevent the use of artificial intelligence to refuse Medicare coverage for medical services. It aims to guarantee that patients receive fair, transparent evaluations of their claims without relying on opaque AI systems.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary pause on building new data centers that power AI services. The goal is to reduce energy use, curb environmental impact, and give lawmakers time to develop more sustainable solutions.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 seeks to protect consumers and workers from unfair practices by AI companies, targeting the abuse of AI technology to inflate prices and manipulate labor markets. The legislation proposes regulations that would limit AI firms from engaging in price gouging and wage fixing, ensuring fair competition and equitable pay for workers.

title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 43 - 0.
summary: The Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 is a proposed U.S. law aimed at tightening protection for AI model intellectual property. It seeks to reduce illicit copying and unauthorized use of AI models by creating stricter penalties and stronger enforcement tools for those who steal or improperly distribute model code and data.

title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026 creates a framework for studying and monitoring how artificial intelligence is used in the judicial system, aiming to keep AI applications transparent, fair, and accountable. It establishes a dedicated research and oversight body that sets guidelines for AI use in courts and requires regular reporting on its effects and compliance.

title: SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship.
summary: The SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026 establishes a framework for small businesses to responsibly adopt and use artificial intelligence, setting standards for safety, transparency, and ethical compliance. It also provides incentives—such as grants and technical support—to help small enterprises integrate AI technologies into their operations while ensuring consumer protection and data privacy.

title: American Artificial Intelligence Leadership and Uniformity Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The American Artificial Intelligence Leadership and Uniformity Act proposes a coordinated national framework to strengthen the United States' position in AI development and deployment, ensuring consistent standards and policies across industries. It emphasizes increased research investment, regulatory alignment, and collaborative efforts to promote innovation while safeguarding safety and competitiveness on a global stage.

title: Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act of 2026 establishes a federal framework for evaluating and mitigating risks that AI systems pose. It requires agencies to assess safety, transparency, and accountability before deploying AI, and sets standards for ongoing monitoring and reporting.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 619.
summary: The act aims to boost the development and use of AI in the financial sector, encouraging innovation and competitive growth. It also establishes a regulatory framework to ensure responsible use, protect data, and safeguard consumers while opening up new opportunities for banks, investors, and fintech firms.

title: HBCU AI Research Leadership Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The HBCU AI Research Leadership Act aims to strengthen AI research and innovation at historically Black colleges and universities. It proposes funding, collaborations, and training programs to establish HBCUs as leaders in artificial intelligence research and education.
